title: Database connection
summary: Connect to PostgreSQL or MongoDB with native drivers in JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, and C#.
overview: Start with a reliable connection, then add safe reads and writes, bounded queries, pooling, indexes, and production configuration. Examples use direct driver APIs with no ORM.

variants.title: PostgreSQL
variants.summary: Relational tables, SQL queries, transactions, and an explicit connection pool.

javascript.introduction: Node.js ESM with the pg driver. Keep one Pool for the process; a Pool owns reusable connections.

sections.heading: Install and prepare
sections.body: Create a database and provide DATABASE_URL through your environment. The sample table stores a unique email and a display name. Run the SQL once with psql or a migration.
sections.code:
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install pg
psql "$DATABASE_URL" <<'SQL'
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name text NOT NULL
);
SQL

sections.heading: Connect and write
sections.body: Create one Pool at startup. Parameter placeholders keep values separate from SQL. End the pool during shutdown; do not end it after every request.

sections.heading: Query further
sections.body: Use parameterized filters, bounded pages, and a checked-out client for transactions. Release that client in finally.

sections.heading: Configure the pool
sections.body: Set a connection limit and timeouts that fit your deployment. In production, use the server certificate and a verified TLS configuration; keep credentials outside source control.

typescript.introduction: Node.js with TypeScript and the pg driver. Types describe result rows while SQL remains explicit.

sections.heading: Install and prepare
sections.body: Initialize a TypeScript project and create the users table shown in the JavaScript tab. Supply DATABASE_URL at runtime.
sections.code:
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install pg
npm install -D typescript @types/node @types/pg
npx tsc --init --module nodenext --target es2022
psql "$DATABASE_URL" <<'SQL'
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name text NOT NULL
);
SQL

sections.heading: Connect and write
sections.body: One Pool serves the application. Use a typed result row and positional parameters.

sections.heading: Query further
sections.body: Use an ordered, limited page; use the same checked-out client for each statement in a transaction.

sections.heading: Configure the pool
sections.body: Size the pool for the database connection budget. Handle errors from idle clients and close the pool at shutdown.

go.introduction: Go with pgx/v5/pgxpool. pgxpool is safe to share between goroutines and supports context cancellation.

sections.heading: Install and prepare
sections.body: Create a Go module, add pgx, and create the users table from the JavaScript tab. Export DATABASE_URL before running.
sections.code:
go mod init example.com/db-demo
go get github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool
psql "$DATABASE_URL" <<'SQL'
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name text NOT NULL
);
SQL

sections.heading: Connect and write
sections.body: Construct the pool once, verify it with Ping, and close it at shutdown. QueryRow reports errors when Scan runs.

sections.heading: Query further
sections.body: The fragment below belongs inside a function returning error. Close rows and check rows.Err after iteration. A transaction must commit or roll back before reuse.

sections.heading: Configure the pool
sections.body: The fragment below belongs inside a function returning error. Parse the URI to set pool bounds. Use request-scoped contexts with deadlines in real handlers.
sections.code:
config, err := pgxpool.ParseConfig(os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"))
if err != nil { return err }
config.MaxConns = 10
config.MinConns = 1
pool, err := pgxpool.NewWithConfig(ctx, config)
if err != nil { return err }
defer pool.Close()

csharp.introduction: C# with Npgsql. Build one NpgsqlDataSource for the application and use parameterized commands.

sections.heading: Install and prepare
sections.body: Create a console app, install Npgsql, and create the users table. Set DATABASE_URL to an Npgsql connection string such as Host=localhost;Database=app;Username=app;Password=... . Adjust the psql host, user, and database to match.
sections.code:
dotnet new console -n DbDemo
cd DbDemo
dotnet add package Npgsql
psql -h localhost -U app -d app <<'SQL'
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name text NOT NULL
);
SQL

sections.heading: Connect and write
sections.body: A data source manages a pool. Positional placeholders keep values out of SQL text.

sections.heading: Query further
sections.body: Use a reader for multiple rows. Use one opened connection and its transaction for related writes.

sections.heading: Configure the pool
sections.body: Set a bounded pool and command timeout in the connection string. Require verified TLS for remote production connections.

variants.title: MongoDB
variants.summary: Documents, typed collections, cursor queries, indexes, and a shared client.

javascript.introduction: Node.js ESM with the official MongoDB driver. Share one MongoClient across the application.

sections.heading: Install and prepare
sections.body: Install the official driver and set MONGODB_URI. MongoDB creates the app database and users collection when first written.
sections.code:
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install mongodb
export MONGODB_URI='mongodb://localhost:27017'

sections.heading: Connect and write
sections.body: Connect once, ping to check reachability, and close on process shutdown. Documents use a unique email field.

sections.heading: Query further
sections.body: Filter and project only the fields needed. Bound result size. An aggregation groups by a field; use update and delete filters for writes.

sections.heading: Configure connection and indexes
sections.body: Index fields used for lookup; a unique index enforces email uniqueness. Size the client pool and set a selection timeout. Use TLS and authentication in the deployment URI.

typescript.introduction: Node.js TypeScript with the official MongoDB driver. A typed collection describes document fields.

sections.heading: Install and prepare
sections.body: Install the driver and TypeScript; set MONGODB_URI. The driver includes its own TypeScript types.
sections.code:
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install mongodb
npm install -D typescript @types/node
npx tsc --init --module nodenext --target es2022

sections.heading: Connect and write
sections.body: Create one MongoClient. Ping makes startup failures visible; close the client at shutdown.

sections.heading: Query further
sections.body: Use bounded cursor results and typed filters. Aggregation output can have a different shape from source documents.

sections.heading: Configure connection and indexes
sections.body: Create the unique index during deployment or startup before accepting writes. Keep credentials in the environment.

go.introduction: Go with the official MongoDB Go driver v2. Share the client and pass a context to operations.

sections.heading: Install and prepare
sections.body: Initialize a module, add the v2 driver, and export MONGODB_URI.
sections.code:
go mod init example.com/db-demo
go get go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/mongo

sections.heading: Connect and write
sections.body: Connect a client, ping it, and disconnect on shutdown. Decode a found document into a typed struct.

sections.heading: Query further
sections.body: Inside a function returning error, use a bounded cursor and check iteration errors. Aggregate groups matching documents; close each cursor. UpdateOne changes only matching documents.

sections.heading: Configure connection and indexes
sections.body: The fragment below belongs inside a function returning error. Bound the pool and create a unique index for email. A context deadline should bound each request operation.

csharp.introduction: C# with the official MongoDB .NET driver. Keep MongoClient as an application singleton.

sections.heading: Install and prepare
sections.body: Create a project, install the driver, and set MONGODB_URI. The app database appears after the first write.
sections.code:
dotnet new console -n DbDemo
cd DbDemo
dotnet add package MongoDB.Driver

sections.heading: Connect and write
sections.body: Get a typed collection and ping to confirm connectivity before accepting requests.

sections.heading: Query further
sections.body: The fluent API supports filters, sort, and limit. Use targeted updates and aggregation for grouped results.

sections.heading: Configure connection and indexes
sections.body: The client already pools connections. Adjust the limit only for your deployment budget; use TLS and credentials in the URI.
